subject: science
passage: House sparrows have declined sharply in many European cities since the 1980s, and the causes remain debated. One explanation blames the loss of nesting cavities as old buildings are renovated; another blames a shortage of the insects that sparrows need to feed their chicks. Urban ecologist Sven Lindgren, who counted sparrows and flying insects and surveyed nesting cavities across twelve neighborhoods of a Scandinavian city, argues that his data favor the second explanation. Neighborhoods with abundant cavities but few insects, he observes, hold scarcely more sparrows than neighborhoods lacking both, whereas insect-rich neighborhoods support many sparrows even where cavities are comparatively scarce.

data.title: Nesting Cavities, Insects, and Sparrows in Twelve City Neighborhoods

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support Lindgren's argument?

choices.A: Neighborhoods with many cavities and many insects had the highest sparrow count, 31 per kilometer of street.
choices.B: Neighborhoods with few cavities held fewer sparrows than those with many cavities regardless of insect abundance.
choices.C: Neighborhoods with many cavities but few insects held only 6 sparrows per kilometer, barely above the 4 found where both were scarce, while insect-rich neighborhoods with few cavities held 24.
choices.D: Renovation of old buildings removed more nesting cavities in insect-poor neighborhoods than in insect-rich ones.

explanation.why: To favor one explanation over the other, Lindgren needs neighborhoods where cavities and insects point in different directions. The evidence must compare the two mixed rows: plenty of cavities but few insects gives 6 sparrows per kilometer, close to the 4 where both are scarce, while few cavities but many insects gives 24.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is true, but a neighborhood rich in both cavities and insects fits either explanation equally well, so it cannot show which factor matters.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Neighborhoods with few cavities but many insects held 24 sparrows per kilometer, far more than the 6 in neighborhoods with many cavities but few insects.
explanation.C: Correct. Cavities without insects yield almost no sparrows, while insects without cavities yield many, which is exactly the pattern that favors the insect explanation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The table reports how many cavities exist, not how or why any were lost.
